chunks: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said:

No, by God! Neither will the command nor the Caliphate ever return to the clan of Abu Bakr and Umar, nor ever to the Banu Umayya, nor ever among the children of Talha and al-Zubayr — and that is because they discarded the Quran, invalidated the Sunnah, and disrupted the rulings.

And the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: The Quran is a guidance from straying, a clarity from blindness, a rescue from stumbling, a light from darkness, an illumination from newly-occurring events, a protection from destruction, a right guidance from temptation, an explanation from strife, and a conveyance from this world to the Hereafter; and in it is the perfection of your religion — and no one deviates from the Quran except toward the Fire.

key_terms.السُّنَنَ: the Sunnah — the prophetic traditions and precedents
key_terms.الْخِلَافَةُ: Caliphate — the political-religious succession to the Prophet
key_terms.كَمَالُ دِينِكُمْ: the perfection of your religion — an echo of Quran 5:3
key_terms.نَبَذُوا: discarded — a strong condemnation meaning 'cast behind their backs'

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the Caliphate returning to Abu Bakr's clan or the Umayyads?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) declares emphatically that legitimate governance will never revert to the early caliphs or the Umayyads, grounding this in their betrayal of Quran and Sunnah. He then quotes the Prophet (SAWW) exalting the Quran as the all-encompassing guide of human life, culminating in the warning that deviation from the Quran leads only to the Fire. This hadith was addressed in a context of Shia political marginalization under Umayyad/Abbasid rule, serving as doctrinal assurance and a call to Quranic fidelity.
